title: Antique Studio Material Conservation Lab
description: You are a virtual material conservator in a vintage photography studio. An antique camera sits on a wooden leather sofa, and you must adjust PBR material properties (roughness, metalness, sheen, color tint, emissive glow, opacity) across both objects while obeying a total 'material energy budget' that is conserved across all channels. Full undo/redo history tracks every adjustment.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads AntiqueCamera.glb placed on top of SheenWoodLeatherSofa.glb in a studio scene. Camera: perspective at (0,1.5,3) looking at origin. Lighting: one warm DirectionalLight, one cool HemisphereLight, and an HDR-less environment via PMREMGenerator from a simple RoomEnvironment. Core mechanic — Material Energy Budget: define a global budget of 6.0 energy units. Six material channels exist: roughness, metalness, sheenIntensity, colorTintStrength (a uniform lerp toward a user-chosen hex color), emissiveIntensity, and opacity. Each channel ranges 0-1 and its energy cost equals its value. The sum across all six channels must always equal exactly 6.0 (conservation law). When the user increases one channel's slider, the remaining five automatically decrease proportionally to maintain the sum. Build a left-side HTML panel with: (1) six labeled range sliders for the channels, (2) a color picker for the tint target color, (3) a toggle to choose whether adjustments apply to the camera meshes, the sofa meshes, or both (multi-input coupling — changes propagate to selected targets), (4) Undo and Redo buttons. Every slider change is a discrete state snapshot pushed onto an undo stack (cap at 50). Redo stack clears on new action. On each change, traverse selected model(s) and for every Mesh set material.roughness, material.metalness, material.sheenIntensity (enable material.sheen=true for sofa), material.emissiveIntensity with material.emissive set from tint color, and material.opacity (material.transparent=true). Display a real-time bar chart (six small colored div bars) showing current energy distribution. The task requires 10-14 deliberate interactions: select target, adjust multiple sliders observing conservation rebalancing, change tint color, switch target, adjust again, then undo/redo several steps to compare looks. Add OrbitControls for scene inspection. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial override on all loaded meshes to support sheen and all PBR channels uniformly.
